title: Optical Overlay Metrology - Voids Detection on C205 Broadband Plasma
subtitle: Post-CMP Quality Validation for 10nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Klaus Weber

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the C205 Broadband Plasma system to detect and classify Voids defects during post-cmp inspection at the 10nm technology node. The test is conducted at Dresden Fab 3 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Voids defects that are critical to yield at the 10nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the C205 Broadband Plasma platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: C205 Broadband Plasma
- Inspection Type: Optical Overlay Metrology
- Target Defect: Voids
- Process Step: Post-CMP
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 10nm
- Fab Location: Dresden Fab 3

This test case applies to all C205 Broadband Plasma systems deployed at Dresden Fab 3 for post-cmp monitoring in the 10nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: C205 Broadband Plasma
Software Version: v8.5.957
Recipe: OPTICAL_OVERLAY_METROLOGY_10nm_POST_CMP
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: High (179 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the C205 Broadband Plasma system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Optical Overlay Metrology' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Voids defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 10nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 48 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 99% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.7% for Optical Overlay Metrology
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.93 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-05-14
Wafers Tested: 5
Total Defects Found: 4288
Defect Density: 1364.91 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 6.3%
Capture Rate: 86.0%
Test Duration: 357 minutes
System Uptime: 97.1%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The C205 Broadband Plasma demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Voids at the 10nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Voids at 10nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
